newsitem.title: UK: Weinstock will work with Simpson at GEC.
newsitem.headline: Weinstock will work with Simpson at GEC.

text.p: He may have stepped down as chief executive and be off the board of "his" GEC, but Lord Arnold Weinstock signalled on Friday that he has no intention of stopping work once George Simpson takes over on Monday.

Simpson, who starts a three-year contract that should leave him several million pounds better off, told reporters at today's annual meeting where his appointment was confirmed that he would enjoy "having Arnie around to pick his brains".

A company source said Weinstock wanted to continue going into the office regularly, in his honorary role as Chairman Emeritus, as he feels he has left some of his work unfinished. "He hopes George will do it, and would like to help him."

In his outgoing address, following a glowing tribute from chairman Lord Prior to his 33 years work in building up the electronics, engineering and defence combine, Weinstock made clear he saw Simpson as a force for continuity, not change.
Leadership of GEC, he said, took "teams of people who trust eachother and can work together -- putting ego behind them."
"I think one of the great qualities of George Simpson is exactly that. He won't be striking out on his own...replacing (GEC) with a peculiarly Simpsonian brand of company," he added.
